arxiv-2209-15235.title: Ram Pressure Stripping and ISM disc Truncation : Prediction vs. Observation 2022 Ram Pressure Stripping and ISM disc Truncation : Prediction vs. Observation –
arxiv-2209-15235.creator: Seona Lee, Yun-Kyeong Sheen, Hyein Yoon, Yara Jaffé, Aeree Chung
arxiv-2209-15235.description: Abstract Ram pressure stripping (RPS) is known to be a key environmental effect that can remove interstellar gas from galaxies in a cluster. The RPS process is commonly described as a competition between the ram pressure by the intracluster medium (ICM) and the anchoring pressure on the interstellar medium (ISM) by the gravitational potential of a galaxy.

arxiv-2309-02803.title: The dyadic Riesz vector II
arxiv-2309-02803.creator: Komla Domelevo, Stefanie Petermichl
arxiv-2309-02803.description: Abstract We derive a dyadic model operator for the Riesz vector. We show linear upper L p \displaystyle L^{p} bounds for 1 < p < ∞ \displaystyle 1<p<\infty between this model operator and the Riesz vector, when applied to functions with values in Banach spaces.

arxiv-2401-00873.title: Unifying Self-Supervised Clustering and Energy-Based Models
arxiv-2401-00873.creator: Emanuele Sansone, Robin Manhaeve
arxiv-2401-00873.description: Abstract Self-supervised learning excels at learning representations from large amounts of data. At the same time, generative models offer the complementary property of learning information about the underlying data generation process. In this study, we aim at establishing a principled connection between these two paradigms and highlight the benefits of their complementarity.

arxiv-2405-02783.title: Linear Noise Approximation Assisted Bayesian Inference on Mechanistic Model of Partially Observed Stochastic Reaction Network
arxiv-2405-02783.creator: Wandi Xu, Wei Xie
arxiv-2405-02783.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wandi Xu, Wei Xie. To support mechanism online learning and facilitate digital twin development for biomanufacturing processes, this paper develops an efficient Bayesian inference approach for partially observed enzymatic stochastic reaction network (SRN), a fundamental building block of multi-scale bioprocess mechanistic model.

arxiv-2408-16574.title: Small deviations of Gaussian multiplicative chaos and the free energy of the two-dimensional massless Sinh–Gordon model
arxiv-2408-16574.creator: Nikolay Barashkov, Joona Oikarinen, Mo Dick Wong
arxiv-2408-16574.description: Abstract We prove a global decomposition result for log \log -correlated Gaussian fields on the d d -dimensional torus and use this to derive new small deviations bounds for a class of Gaussian multiplicative chaos measures obtained from Gaussian fields with zero spatial mean on the d d -dimensional torus.

arxiv-2409-00972.title: A potential energy conserving finite element method for turbulent variable density flow: application to glacier-fjord circulation
arxiv-2409-00972.creator: Lukas Lundgren, Christian Helanow, Jonathan Wiskandt, Inga Monika Koszalka, Josefin Ahlkrona
arxiv-2409-00972.description: Abstract We introduce a continuous Galerkin finite element discretization of the non-hydrostatic Boussinesq approximation of the Navier-Stokes equations, suitable for various applications such as coastal ocean dynamics and ice-ocean interactions, among others. In particular, we introduce a consistent modification of the gravity force term which enhances conservation properties for Galerkin methods without strictly enforcing the divergence-free condition.

arxiv-2410-02217.title: Stochastic Sampling from Deterministic Flow Models
arxiv-2410-02217.creator: Saurabh Singh, Ian Fischer
arxiv-2410-02217.description: Abstract Deterministic flow models, such as rectified flows, offer a general framework for learning a deterministic transport map between two distributions, realized as the vector field for an ordinary differential equation (ODE). However, they are sensitive to model estimation and discretization errors and do not permit different samples conditioned on an intermediate state, limiting their application.

pmc-10672488.title: Shrinkage, Permeation and Freeze–Thaw Characteristics of Ambient Cured High Calcium-Based Alkali-Activated Engineered Composites
pmc-10672488.creator: Khandaker M A Hossain, Dhruv Sood, Mohammad Saberian
pmc-10672488.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Sustainable zero cement-based one-part ambient cured alkali-activated engineered composites (AAECs) are developed. The durability and microstructural characteristics of developed AAECs using 2% v/v polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) fibers, silica sand, binary or ternary combinations of precursors (fly ash class C ‘FA-C’, fly ash class F ‘FA-F’ and ground granulated blast furnace slag ‘GGBFS’) and two types of powder form alkaline reagents (Type 1 and Type 2) are evaluated compared to conventional engineered cementitious composites (ECCs) and alkali-activated mortars (AAMs) without fiber.

pmc-11586894.title: Overexpression of enhanced yellow fluorescent protein fused with Channelrhodopsin‐2 causes contractile dysfunction in skeletal muscle
pmc-11586894.creator: Syeda N Lamia, Carol S Davis, Peter C D Macpherson, T Brad Willingham, Yingfan Zhang, Chengyu Liu, Leanne Iannucci, Elahe Ganji, Desmond Harden, Iman Bhattacharya, Adam C Abraham, Susan V Brooks, Brian Glancy, Megan L Killian
pmc-11586894.description: Skeletal muscle activation using optogenetics has emerged as a promising technique for inducing noninvasive muscle contraction and assessing muscle function both in vivo and in vitro. Transgenic mice overexpressing the optogenetic fusion protein, Channelrhodopsin 2‐EYFP (ChR2‐EYFP) in skeletal muscle are widely used; however, overexpression of fluorescent proteins can negatively impact the functionality of activable tissues.

pmc-12575644.title: Video based heart rate detection in unrestrained laboratory rats: a feasibility analysis
pmc-12575644.creator: Julianna Monissen, Lucas Mösch, Matthias Monissen, Laura Warner, Ute Lindauer, Michael Czaplik, Carina Barbosa Pereira
pmc-12575644.description: Continuous monitoring of vital signs in laboratory animals is often essential for reliable scientific results and severity assessment. It still depends on invasive approaches such as transponder implementation, which affect the animals well-being. To minimize this impact, a camera-based method is proposed for heart rate detection by analyzing skin color variations in unrestrained rats.

pmc-12577156.title: Ventricular septum curvature ratio: a novel imaging marker to predict clinical deterioration in normotensive acute pulmonary embolism
pmc-12577156.creator: Yizhuo Gao, Zhichun Gu, Xuejiao Wei, Shibo Wei, Yuchen Liu, Shanshan Zhan, Jing Yang, Chuanxin Qi, Shougang Qi, Minggang Wang, Dong Jia
pmc-12577156.description: BackgroundIdentifying high-probability deterioration individuals at the time of admission remains a challenge in normotensive patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE). Ventricular septum (VS) deviation, as observed on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA), has been associated with poor prognosis in acute PE patients.

pmc-12705850.title: Resting after learning or repeating the learned?
pmc-12705850.creator: Markus Martini, Tom Mercer, Luis Gutmann, Stephan Frederic Dahm, Robert Marhenke, Pierre Sachse
pmc-12705850.description: The formation of new memories can be influenced by the activities that immediately follow learning. Previous research has shown that several minutes of wakeful resting after learning can enhance memory retention compared to engaging in unrelated tasks, likely by facilitating memory consolidation.

pmc-12722372.title: From monochromatic waves to realistic tides: deep learning for short-term forecasting of coastal ocean
pmc-12722372.creator: Irem Yildiz, Emil V. Stanev, Joanna Staneva
pmc-12722372.description: In this study, a hybrid architecture combining convolutional neural networks for spatial reconstruction and long short-term memory networks for temporal forecasting is used to predict sea-level variations in the German Bight. This new framework is applied to a series of sea level data ranging from academic to realistic data.

pmc-13137939.title: Global burden, risk factors and projections of self‐harm mortality in adults aged 65+ years: A 60‐year trend analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
pmc-13137939.creator: Jinjie Xu, Yiman Guo, Zizhao Feng, Meiti Wang, Chengwei Guo, Yuan Feng
pmc-13137939.description: BackgroundEpidemiological research on self‐harm in older adults (aged 65+ years) remains scarce despite its growing public health significance amid global ageing.AimsThis study aimed to analyse the global burden, risk factors and projections of self‐harm mortality in adults aged 65+ years from 1990 to 2050.

pmc-13187442.title: SVRS: self-supervised 3D voxel reconstruction network from stereo vision
pmc-13187442.creator: Zhengyang Zou, Yunxia Wu, Hailan Zhang, Qian Xu, Ruifeng Wang
pmc-13187442.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Three-dimensional voxel reconstruction based on stereo vision is essential for environmental perception in autonomous robots. Existing pseudo-LiDAR methods recover voxel grids by estimating depth maps and projecting them pixel by pixel, leading to high computational cost and boundary over-smoothing. To overcome these issues, we model the inverse relationship between 2D pixels and 3D voxel grids and propose a Self-supervised 3D Voxel Reconstruction network from Stereo vision (SVRS).

IntroductionFoslevodopa/foscarbidopa (LDp/CDp) is a nonsurgical 24-h continuous subcutaneous infusion for patients with advanced Parkinson’s disease (aPD) and motor fluctuations uncontrolled on oral medications. We present the first multicountry real-world data from routine clinical practice.MethodsROSSINI (NCT06107426) is an ongoing 3-year multicountry, prospective, observational study of adults with aPD who are LDp/CDp-naïve (cohort A) or transitioning from LDp/CDp open-label extension studies (NCT04379050/NCT04750226, cohort B).
